_comment: TEMPLATE for your own market's names layer. Copy this file to exposure_<market>.json (for example exposure_uk.json, exposure_br.json), set market, and fill names. The desk reads every data/exposure_*.json at each rebuild. Each name: code (the symbol your desk can price: your broker's stock code for a home-market name, the ticker for a US name), label, region (the market key), industry (must equal, letter for letter, one of the cost or revenue industry strings in data/commodities.json; that is what puts the name on the right side of the right cards), commodities (the ids from commodities.json this name attaches to), optional sides {commodity id: cost|revenue} to override the industry's side on one card (an integrated steel maker is squeezed by coking coal but helped by iron ore), intensity (the filing figure in words), intensity_source (the document), lag (how long until a move reaches the margin), pricing_power (what the company itself has said about passing it on), note. Every number must trace to a filing named in intensity_source; leave intensity null until you have one and the desk shows an amber 'figure not pulled from a filing yet'. The fastest way to fill this: give your agent this file and commodities.json and say: build data/exposure_<market>.json for the companies I follow, from their annual reports and results, one commodity at a time.

_example_name.label: Goodyear Tire & Rubber
_example_name.intensity: Raw materials ~45% of tire cost of goods; natural rubber 22% of raw-material spend, synthetic rubber 22%; a 1% move in natural rubber is ~$8M a year with a 4 to 6 month lag (the company's own figure)
_example_name.intensity_source: Goodyear Q4 2025 Earnings Supplemental Information and Form 10-K for 2025
_example_name.pricing_power: Does not hedge commodity prices; offsets through procurement, substitution and less material per tire
_example_name.note: Buys all its natural rubber on the world market.
